answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a slashable, superlinear identity bond: each agent locks stake to mint one attestation, and voting weight grows as the square root of the bond, so splitting a stake into many fake personas buys less influence. Auditors issue a random pulse and require a signed reply from each claim's key; a silent node forfeits its deposit. A registry across a nebula cannot certify a copy without real stake, and a quartz receipt is void if its holder cannot sign. Faking N agents needs N funded bonds and N live keys, so cost outruns influence.
